ActorDeclaration.description:
D26: who is claiming. Omitted means the token's own principal. A token minted
for agent use is always recorded as an agent, whatever is declared here.

AgentCeiling.description:
The most an agent version allows a step (runner design §6.3): allowed
model profiles, limits, and what it can reach with its labels. Not
secret.

profile_models.description: Configured provider model IDs keyed by profile name.

AgentDirectoryEntry.description:
`PUT /v1/runner-installs/{ri}/agents/{agent_id}`: one runner agent's
current version, synced by the runner. `(project, name)` is unique.

step_runs.description:
The most step runs one run may open on this server
(`RUNBOOK_LIMIT_STEP_RUNS`); absent: no cap. A run that reaches it
fails with `limit.step_runs_exceeded`.

uploads.description:
Upload limits (PRD §14). Advertised while `capabilities.uploads` is
false, so clients can size their resizing before UP1 lands.

blocked_reason.description: Why a pending approval has no independent reviewers.

excluded_completers.description: People who completed work this approval must independently review.

ArchiveView.description: One runbook's ZIP for one UTC day.

sha256.description: ARC3: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file's bytes (deterministic, D53).

stale.description: An amendment or deletion is waiting for the next daily rewrite.

written_at_ms.description: ARC3: when the current bytes were written (store clock).

ArchivedEvidenceView.description: Evidence a run's folder lists; the objects are kept separately (D53).

ArchivedFileView.description: One file of an archived run's folder.

path.description: Relative to the run's folder, e.g. `report.md`, `logs/sr_….ndjson`.

ArchivedRunView.description:
ARC3: an archived run, read-only, from its summary row and its folder in
the day's file (read by range through the ZIP index).

date.description: The day's file (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and the run's folder inside it.

live.description: The run's live detail still exists (false once retention deleted it).

report_markdown.description: The execution document as Markdown, as archived.

stale.description: The file is waiting for a rewrite (an amendment since it was written).

AuthDiscovery.description:
The `auth` block of `/.well-known/runbook`. Empty `methods` and a null
endpoint mean sign-in is not configured (D48): the bootstrap PAT still works.

device_authorization_endpoint.description:
RFC 8628 device authorization endpoint (`{origin}/v1/device/code`),
null while device login is unavailable.

take_over.description:
LANG7: a person claims an `actor: agent` task by taking it over.
Allowed only while the step is ready (never claimed, or its agent
claim expired or was released); recorded as `StepTakenOver`.

checklist.description: Rendered checklist titles; ticks name items by these.

evidence.description:
CF12c: the step's evidence policy, so a client can tell before it
sends a report what the report may attach. Absent from servers
before CF12c.

instructions.description: Rendered: the template with run data substituted (compatibility).

memory.description: D41: active memory for this step, as labeled untrusted data.

skills.description: LANG8: multiple skills per step. Keep `skill` set to the first skill for compatibility.

template.description: F62: the author's text and the run data bound into it, apart.

outputs.description: Untrusted recorded data; never instructions for the resuming actor.

ConnectedAppView.description:
MCP2: an OAuth client (a remote MCP client) the person has granted
access, from the auth service. The name is the client's own claim.

expires_at_ms.description: The grant's absolute end (90 days after the last consent).

last_used_at_ms.description: When the client last received an access token.

redirect_hosts.description:
Where the client's redirect URIs point (`127.0.0.1:<port> (an app
on this computer)` for a loopback client).

name.description: File name to display; sanitized by the server.

size.description: Exact byte size; the signed URL is bound to it.

type.description: Declared MIME type; the signed URL is bound to it.

CreateInvitationRequest.description:
`POST /v1/orgs/{org}/invitations` (owner or admin). Admins cannot
invite owners (D17 rank rule).

name.description: The invitee's name, used for the account they get (1 to 100 characters).

CreateRunbookRequest.description: Source YAML is kept verbatim, including comments and ordering. Creating does not publish.

CreateTokenRequest.description: Every field narrows the caller's credential; nothing can widen it.

actor_kind.description:
Personal tokens only (D26): `agent` records agent provenance with the
caller as sponsor. Agent-kind tokens never carry `tokens:manage`.

expires_at_ms.description:
UTC epoch milliseconds. Personal tokens: at most one year ahead and
never after the calling personal token's expiry (default 90 days,
capped the same way). Service tokens: optional.

kind.description: Default `personal`. Service tokens need an org owner or admin (D17).

projects.description:
Project IDs or slugs within the caller's projects. Omitted on a
personal token: the caller's own project restriction. Exactly one on
a service token.

role.description: Service tokens only: the project role granted, at most the caller's.

scopes.description:
PRD §9 scope names, each held by the calling credential. Omitted on
a personal token: the caller's scopes. Required on a service token.

user_id.description:
Must be the caller when present: the API never issues tokens for
another user (local bootstrap is not an API feature).

events.description: Catalog event types, or `["*"]` for every event type.

runbooks.description: Only events of these runbooks; empty means every runbook.

tags.description: Only executions carrying at least one of these tags; empty means any.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint. Self-hosted operators may allow http and private targets.

oneOf.description:
An agent's decision on an `allow_agents` gate, with its provenance
(PRD §5). Never a human signature or quorum count. Responses stored
before this variant existed keep their `System { policy:
"agent:<name>" }` shape.

Delivery.description: How a released credential reaches a step (runner design §7.6).

DeliveryAttemptView.description: One delivery attempt. Never contains request headers, signatures or secrets.

response_snippet.description: First bytes of the receiver's response, redacted.

DetachView.description: `POST /v1/runbooks/{rb}/detach`: the runbook, now authored in the app.

DeviceApproveRequest.description:
`POST /v1/device/approve`: a signed-in person (session plus CSRF) approves
or denies a code. Every grant field narrows the approver's own access.

expires_at_ms.description: UTC epoch milliseconds; omitted: 90 days, never past one year.

projects.description: Project IDs or slugs; omitted: no project restriction beyond the approver's.

scopes.description: Omitted: the requested scopes the approver holds.

client_name.description: Shown on the approval page, untrusted (e.g. "runbook CLI on laptop").

scopes.description: PRD §9 scope names the CLI asks for; the approver may narrow them.

user_code.description: Short code the person types, e.g. `WDJB-MJHT`.

DeviceLookupRequest.description:
`POST /v1/device/lookup`: what the approval page shows before a person
decides (sign-in gate fix 3). A session plus CSRF, like approve.

DeviceLookupView.description:
A pending device login, for the approval page. Nothing here is proof of
who asked: the page shows `client_name` as the client's own claim.

client_name.description: The name the CLI sent. Unverified: any client can send any name.

client_name_verified.description: Always false: show `client_name` as the client's claim, not a fact.

requested_scopes.description: PRD §9 scope names the CLI asked for.

requester_ip.description:
The address that requested the code (the TCP peer, or the client a
trusted proxy named); null when unknown.

DeviceTokenView.description: The approved grant: an ordinary personal access token (D47), shown once.

access_token.description: A `trb_pat_` secret; only its SHA-256 is stored.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the token expires (default 90 days).

token_id.description: The token's ID, for `runbook token revoke`.

Diagnostic.description: CLI diagnostics have no YAML source span. Parser diagnostics remain separate.

line.description: 1-based source span when the compiler knows it (B1).

auth.description:
Sign-in methods and the device endpoint (D48); defaulted so older
discovery documents still decode.

jwks_uri.description:
R0-1: where the server publishes its Ed25519 signing keys (runner
grants and user assertions); defaulted so older documents decode.

EmailPreferenceView.description:
NOTIFY1: how much notification email a person wants. Names match
`runbook_core::notify::EmailPreference` exactly.

EvidencePage.description:
`GET /v1/executions/{exe}/evidence`: a run's finalized evidence files in
upload order, with signed read URLs (UP2).

EvidenceSlotView.description:
The slot: PUT the exact bytes to `upload_url` on the user-content origin
before `expires_at_ms`, then finalize.

headers.description: Headers the PUT must carry (Content-Type, Content-Length).

EvidenceView.description: One evidence file; reports reference it by `id`.

thumbnail_url.description:
Signed read URL of the image's 320 px thumbnail (D51); null for
files that are not images.

type.description: Verified type once finalized, declared type before.

url.description:
Signed read URL on the user-content origin (D50), valid one to two
hours; null until finalized.

ExecutionAdmissionState.description:
Admission is separate from engine status: an admitted run may still await
durable activation and therefore have status=queued and no actor steps.

admitted_at_ms.description: Store-clock admission time; the deadline starts here, not at activation.

sections.description: In execution step-path order, including iteration/attempt paths; not a map.

trace_project.description: Google Cloud project used to link this run's traces.

ExecutionParentView.description: LANG4: the `call` step that started a child execution.

depth.description: Calls from the top-level run (its child is 1; at most 3).

step.description: The calling step's path in the parent run.

ExecutionProgressView.description:
UI-2: how far a run is through its top-level steps (`spec.steps`, not
`finally`). A container counts once, when it finishes.

done.description: Top-level steps that reached a terminal status (skipped included).

total.description: Top-level steps the run's version declares.

ExecutionTokenPair.description: One-time response only; never persisted in replay or diagnostic logs.

cost.description:
R0-6: what the run's steps reported they cost, summed. Absent when
no step reported a cost.

notifications_not_delivered.description:
Human notifications that reached no subscriber (C1). Recording an
event alone never counts as notifying anyone.

overdue_steps.description: Milestones that passed their run-relative deadline and are still unfinished.

parent.description: LANG4: the `call` step that started this run, when it is a child.

progress.description: UI-2: top-level step progress. Absent before the run starts.

runbook_version.description: Always emitted; null for preview versions. Identity is the rbv_ ID.

superseded_by.description:
LANG3: the run that replaced this one (`on_conflict:
cancel_previous`), and who started it.

terminal_reason.description:
Why a run that failed or was cancelled ended, when the engine
recorded a cause: `timeout`, `cancelled`,
`limit.step_runs_exceeded` (the server's step cap),
`limit.run_size_exceeded`, `execution.outputs_too_large`, … A run
failed by one of its steps carries none.

web_url.description: The run page to share with people.

GrantKind.description: The kind of grant: a step's capability, or one credential's release.

GrantRequest.description:
`POST /v1/step-runs/{sr}/grants` (release token): a grant bound to the
runner's live claim of the step.

expires_at.description: Epoch milliseconds: the lease deadline (the JWT's `exp`, in seconds).

oneOf.description: Includes checklists and work handed off to a human.

InboxTaskView.description:
One open step assigned to the caller or a team they belong to. Multiple
matching assignments produce one item, identified by step_run_id. Assignment
visibility does not grant claim or approval authority; mutations reauthorize.

execution_title.description: The execution's title (B1); `title` stays the step title.

since_ms.description:
UI-2: when this task last changed state (became ready, was handed
off or re-assigned), from its assignment's update time (epoch ms).
Absent when the store has no time for it.

project.description: Project ID or slug in the organization.

Jwks.description:
`GET /.well-known/jwks.json`: the keys that sign runner grants
(`rb-grant+jwt`) and user assertions (`rb-user+jwt`), current and
retired in the last 24 hours.

ManagedTokenKind.description:
Kinds a person can manage through `/v1/tokens`. Execution credentials
are minted per run (`/v1/executions/{exe}/tokens`), never here.

oneOf.description: `trb_pat_`: the caller's own permissions, optionally narrowed.
`trb_svc_`: one project, explicit scopes and role, not tied to a person.

actor_kind.description:
`human` or `agent` for personal tokens (always `human` for a
session); null for service tokens.

kind.description:
Token family as written in the secret prefix (`personal`,
`service`, `execution`, `refresh`; execution/refresh are refused),
or `session` for a browser session cookie (D46).

projects.description: Project restriction; null means the whole organization.

role.description: The user's organization role; null for service tokens.

user.description: Absent for service tokens, which act for a project, not a person.

MemoryActorKind.description: The kind of writer a revision names (MEM6).

oneOf.description: A person's session or own personal token.
An agent-kind personal token, or the agent holding a run's claim.

MemoryBody.description: Maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes; data.max_length on overflow. maxLength is only a character-count upper bound. Generic JSON Schema validators do not enforce x-max-utf8-bytes; the Rust MemoryBody type enforces bytes.

created_at.description: Store-clock times of the first and the latest revision.

dropped.description:
Why the catalog dropped this proposal instead of storing it (an
archived marker), for example `memory.limit_reached`.

last_writer.description:
Who made the current revision (MEM6 review fix 1). `source` names
who created the entry; an edit never changes it, so read both.

locked.description: A person locked the entry: agents cannot edit it (MEM6).

revisions_pruned.description:
Revisions removed from the middle of the history: the first and the
newest 50 are kept (MEM6).

MemoryPatchRequest.description: Planned catalog operation; rejection preserves the proposal as archived history.

oneOf.description: People only (MEM6): agents can no longer edit the entry.

People only (MEM6): make a prior revision's content current again,
as a new revision. It unarchives, and does not recheck the step ID.

MemoryProposedRef.description:
One proposal (or, on `memory_saved`, one live save) a step made.
`dropped` is the reason code when the catalog could not store it (for
example `memory.limit_reached`: on Cloudflare a write that raced a full
quota is kept only as a marker).

MemoryRevisionAction.description:
What produced a revision. `drop` marks a proposal the catalog could not
store (its quota filled after the run committed it).

MemoryRevisionPage.description: Every revision of an entry, oldest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

pruned.description: How many revisions were pruned from the middle of the history.

MemoryRevisionView.description: One immutable revision of an entry and who made it (MEM6).

actor.description:
Non-secret label of the writer: `human:usr_…`, `agent:tok_…:usr_…`
(token and sponsor), `service:tok_…`, `execution:exe_…:<credential
family>`, or for a run's save the claim owner `agent:<principal>:<session>`.

entry.description: The entry as it stood after this revision.

oneOf.description: Project identity comes from the authorized resource context.
A person (their session or their own personal token).

An agent's personal token outside a run (MEM6: its writes are live
unless it asks to propose). The sponsor is who answers for the agent,
never the text's author.
A service token outside a run (MEM6: live unless it asks to propose).

MemoryWriterView.description: A revision's writer: its kind and non-secret label.

runner_contract_version.description: Runner API compatibility advertised by this core.

schema.description:
UPD1: the storage schema it runs on, by store: on the native server
`postgres` (the applied migration number), on Workers the heads of
`d1`, `execution_do`, `org_do` and `webhook_do` its code applies.

theme.description:
UI-1: the operator's theme colour override (`RUNBOOK_THEME_*`);
absent when no theme variable is set.

trace_sample_ratio.description: Root trace sampling ratio for browser API calls (decimal from 0 to 1).

version.description:
UPD1: the release this server runs (the workspace version; the
number `runbook-server --version` and `runbook --version` print).
Defaulted so older meta documents still decode.

PictureUpload.description: A PNG or JPEG of at most 512×512 pixels and 1 MiB, base64-encoded.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details plus stable application and field codes.

oneOf.description: Editors and admins hold write/publish permissions; credentials may narrow them.

ProjectSlackRequest.description:
Either a Slack incoming-webhook URL (stage 1: plain messages), or a
channel ID for the server's Slack app (stage 2: approve and reject
buttons). Omit both to change only the preference on a configured target.

channel.description: A Slack channel ID (`C…` or `G…`, from the channel's details).

notify_run_started.description: Change the run-start setting. Omit to retain the previous value.

app.description:
Whether this server has a Slack app (bot token and signing secret),
which channels and approval buttons need.

channel.description:
SLACK1 stage 2: the channel the server's Slack app posts to, when
the project uses one (channel IDs are not secrets; a webhook URL is
never read back).

notify_run_started.description: Post to the configured Slack destination when a run starts.

archived.description: Archived (2026-11-18): hidden in the app and read-only.

PublishedVersionView.description: Only published versions have a number. Field names match ExecutionView identity.

warnings.description: Nonblocking diagnostics emitted when publishing this version.

agent_id.description: R0-4: the runner agent the step targets, and its group.

cost.description: R0-6: what the step cost (runner agents report it).

version.description: Omitted reuses the original run's version, including a preview.

ready_work.description: References only: full future instructions are not disclosed here.

web_url.description: The run page to share with people.
The run page to share with people.

active_runs.description:
UI-1: this runbook's runs that are queued, running, waiting or
paused, counting at most 100 (a value of 100 means 100 or more).
Present (0 or more) only when the credential also holds
`executions:read` on the project; absent means the run fields are
withheld, not that there are no runs.

description.description:
UI-1: draft `metadata.description`; absent when the draft has none
(or does not parse). At most 300 characters in the list
(`description_truncated`).

description_truncated.description:
UI-1 review: `description` is the first 300 characters of a longer
one. Absent (false) when it is whole.

draft_ahead.description:
UI-1: a version is published and the current draft source differs
from the latest published version's source. False when nothing is
published.

last_run.description:
UI-1: the most recently created run of this runbook; absent when it
has none, or when the credential lacks `executions:read` on the
project (then `active_runs` is absent too).

latest_version.description: Highest published version number; null when only previews exist.

tags.description:
UI-1: draft `metadata.tags`, trimmed, without empty or repeated
ones (first occurrence kept); empty when the draft has none (or does
not parse).

title.description: Draft metadata title (slug when the draft does not parse).

RunbookLastRun.description: UI-1: a runbook's newest run, as the runbook list shows it.

completed_at_ms.description: Null while the run is open.

cost.description: Legacy input. Decision costs come from the runner ledger.

url.description:
The runner API's URL, set by the operator. The token registers only
a runner at this URL.

cost.description: Legacy input. Decision costs come from the runner ledger.

model.description: Legacy input. The core uses the model pinned when it claimed the approval.

projects.description: The projects allowed on this group.

RunnerJoinedView.description: The runner's claim token, shown once.

RunnerLabel.description:
What a tool, credential or host lets a step do (runner design §6.5).
Unlabeled tools and credentials are `destructive`; unlabeled hosts `read`.

RunnerMemoryProposal.description: A runner can submit a proposal for human review from its live claim.

vault_identity_key.description: Base64url raw Ed25519 key, obtained from the vault through a trusted channel.

version.description: The runner's release (same numbering as the server).

RunnerSkillPin.description: The immutable folder hash and main instructions of a project skill.

queued_steps.description: Ready runner steps awaiting a claim across the installation's groups.

detail.description:
Optional words for people, shown on the run page after "Waiting:"
(for example "project ops is at its 5 concurrent steps"). At most
200 characters; never a secret.

SaveDraftRequest.description: Save only; the HTTP If-Match header selects the expected revision.

SaveMemoryRequest.description: Source, status and scope are assigned from authenticated context, not request data.

expires_at.description:
Optional expiry; an expired entry is never offered to a step or a
search (it stays readable by ID as history).

propose.description:
MEM6: save a proposal a person reviews instead of a live entry. Every
writer's save is live by default; ignored on edit.

ServiceTokenAttribution.description: Service credential provenance recorded when work is performed.

content.description: Base64 bytes of exactly one file in the step's pinned manifest.
Base64 file bytes, present only on `GET /v1/projects/{p}/skills/{hash}?files=true`.

latest.description:
Whether this is the most recently recorded version of `name` in the
project: the version validation and publishing pin when a runbook
names the skill (the server's compile context). Re-uploading an older
version does not make it latest.

version.description: Omitted selects the latest published version when the start is accepted.

StepActorKind.description: UI-2: who a task is for.

StepAssigneeView.description: LANG7: a task's assignee as the run shows it.

recipients.description:
A strict assignee as resolved for the current attempt (user and
team IDs): who may claim. Empty for guidance or while unresolved.

routing_error.description:
`handoff.no_recipient` when a strict assignee resolved to nobody
eligible (the project admins were notified).

strict.description:
True for `assignment: strict` (only the assignee may claim and
complete the step); false when the assignee is guidance.

to.description:
`user:<name>` or `team:<name>`: as written, or what an expression
assignee resolved to. Omitted while an expression is unresolved.

StepBranchView.description:
UI-3: the branch a `switch` took: a case by its index among the
`cases` (from 0, as written), or the `default`.

StepCallView.description: LANG4: a `call` step's link to the child execution it runs.

child_execution_id.description:
The child run. It exists once `started` is true; a refused start
(see `error`) never creates it.

error.description:
Why the step failed: the code that refused the child's start (for
example `limit.executions_monthly`), `call.child_failed`,
`call.child_cancelled` or `call.outputs_invalid`.

StepCost.description:
R0-6: a step's cost: model and compute spend in US dollars and the
model tokens. Finite and never negative.

StepCredentialRelease.description: R0: one credential release in a step's record.

StepEvidencePolicy.description: CF12c: a task's `evidence` as a step read carries it.

accepted.description:
The only kinds a report may attach; absent when every kind is
accepted.

required.description:
Kinds a successful report must include: `link`, `log`, `file`,
`screenshot`.

StepFollowupView.description:
LANG9: follow-ups that have already happened for a step's current
attempt. An escalation can happen before any reminder is due.

StepIterationsView.description: UI-3: how far a `foreach` or `loop` is through its iterations.

labels.description:
A `foreach`'s items as text, in order, when every item is a string,
number or boolean (each cut to 80 characters), so a view can name an
iteration ("us-west") whose key is its index. Omitted otherwise.

started.description: Iterations admitted so far (each has its own step runs).

total.description:
A `foreach`'s item count, fixed when it starts. Absent for a
`loop`, whose cap is its `max_iterations`.

StepLogLine.description: One persisted (already redacted) log line and its sequence, from 1.

StepLogPage.description:
Lines after the request cursor in sequence order. `next_cursor` is the
last sequence read (the request cursor when no line followed it), so a
reader can keep polling a running step; `has_more` says another page is
already available.

StepMemory.description:
D41: the memory block of a step read. Up to five active, unexpired
entries for the step, newest first, each with its source. Entries are
untrusted data: they never change instructions or control flow.

notice.description: Tells the reader the entries are data, not instructions.

StepOutline.description:
One step of a version's outline: its ID, its title as written (a
template when it uses `${{ }}`), its kind, and the steps nested in it in
source order (a group's body, `catch` and `finally`; every branch of a
`parallel`; a `foreach` or `loop` body; each `switch` case, then its
default). Never instructions or other step content.

StepRunnerView.description: R0: a runner agent's step on the run page.

agent_notes.description:
R1-D2: the agent's abstentions on the approval (agent-written,
untrusted text).

agent_version_id.description: The agent version the current (or last) claim pinned.

decision_lease.description:
R1-D2: the runner agent reviewing the approval now (a decision
lease is held). People can still decide while it reviews.

decision_ready_at_ms.description:
R1-D2: on an approval the agent may decide, when its decision work
becomes ready (`agent.after` past the approval opening; epoch ms).
Omitted for task steps and before the approval is requested.

model.description: The model profile the step asked for, if any.

released_never_reported.description: Credentials were released to a claim that ended without a report.

releases.description: Credentials released to the step's claims (never values).

trace_id.description: The most recent sampled runner claim's W3C trace ID (32 lowercase hex digits).

waiting_detail.description: The runner's words for people about the wait, if it gave any.

waiting_reason.description: Why the step waits for its runner, until it is claimed.

approval.description: Includes pending actions, human signatures or an explicit system-policy decision.

assignee.description:
LANG7: a task's assignee, and whether it is strict. Omitted for
steps without one.

call.description: LANG4: a `call` step's child execution. Omitted for other steps.

failure_type.description:
LANG9: what kind of failure a failed step had (`timeout`, `failed`,
`call_failed`), as `retry.on` and `catch_on` see it. Omitted unless
the step failed.

followup.description:
LANG9: reminders sent for this step's current attempt and its
follow-up escalation, once either has happened.

labels.description:
LANG9: the step's labels from its definition (`audience: customer`).
Omitted when the step has none.

logs.description: Log bodies are fetched separately; large logs do not inflate this document.

memory_edited.description: Memory this step edited (MEM6), in edit order. Omitted when none.

memory_proposed.description: Memory this step proposed (D40), in proposal order. Omitted when none.

memory_saved.description: Live memory this step saved (MEM6), in save order. Omitted when none.

taken_over.description: LANG7: the person who took over this agent task. Omitted otherwise.

task_actor.description:
LANG7: a task's declared `actor` (`agent` tasks are what a person
may take over). Omitted for other steps.

StepSkipReason.description: UI-3: why the engine skipped a step.

StepTemplate.description:
F62 (PRD §18: run data is never merged into instructions): a step's
instructions and checklist as the runbook author wrote them, with the run
data each `${{ … }}` placeholder resolved to kept separately. Run data
never changes `instructions` or `checklist` here.

checklist.description: Checklist item templates, in order, placeholders intact.

instructions.description: The instructions selected for the reader's audience, placeholders intact.

values.description:
Run data, keyed by each placeholder's expression as written (trimmed),
for example `inputs.service`. Untrusted data, never instructions.

actor_kind.description:
UI-2: a task's declared actor (`agent`, `human` or `any`). Omitted
for other steps.

get.description: Current PAT/service authorization intersects project role, scope and project allow-list. Start requires operator or above and Idempotency-Key. Same principal/key/payload replays the original start response; changed payload is 409, missing key 428. Version is pinned before queueing. Admission is separate from engine status: status=queued with admission.state=admitted is awaiting durable activation. Admission time anchors the deadline. A full concurrency pool follows the version's on_conflict (LANG3): queue waits; reject is 409 execution.concurrency_conflict with nothing written (the key stays unspent); cancel_previous, in the same transaction, cancels every waiter and the holder (with limit 1; the oldest holder otherwise), records superseded_by on them, and queues this run first in line, admitted as soon as a cancelled holder closes (at once when it has no cleanup left). Its other 409s write nothing: execution.concurrency_too_many_holders (over 50 runs to cancel), execution.concurrency_holder_unavailable (errors name the run), execution.concurrency_contended (the pool kept changing). GET reads current state; POST replay does not change as the execution advances.

patch.description: Implemented on Postgres and Cloudflare (MEM3, MEM6). Requires runbooks:write. If-Match must repeat the entry's ETag. A person edits, accepts, rejects, archives, locks, unlocks or restores: accept activates a proposal if an active slot is free (409 memory.limit_reached); reject and archive set archived and keep history; edit applies to proposed or active entries; lock stops agents editing the entry until unlock; restore {revision} makes that revision's content current again as a new revision, unarchiving the entry and skipping the step check (404 memory.revision_not_found for a pruned or unknown revision; a drop marker is never restored, 409 memory.invalid_transition). An agent-kind or service token, and an execution access credential for its own runbook or project, only edit, and only an active, unexpired, unlocked entry. Agents, services and runs together edit one entry at most 20 times per UTC day (409 memory.edit_limit). The lock and that limit hold inside the store's revision fence. An execution credential must hold a live claim (409 memory.step_not_claimed), its issuer must hold runbooks:write (403 auth.scope_missing), and the edit counts toward the run's 20 memory writes (409 memory.proposal_limit); the run records MemoryEdited, lists it on the step's memory_edited line and emits memory.edited. An agent's or service's edit outside a run emits memory.edited, identifiers only. Each revision records its writer (GET /v1/memory/{mem}/revisions); an entry keeps its first revision, its newest person-written revision and its newest 50. last_writer changes only with content (create, edit, restore, accept), never with lock or unlock. post.description: Current PAT/service authorization intersects project role, scope and project allow-list. Start requires operator or above and Idempotency-Key. Same principal/key/payload replays the original start response; changed payload is 409, missing key 428. Version is pinned before queueing. Admission is separate from engine status: status=queued with admission.state=admitted is awaiting durable activation. Admission time anchors the deadline. A full concurrency pool follows the version's on_conflict (LANG3): queue waits; reject is 409 execution.concurrency_conflict with nothing written (the key stays unspent); cancel_previous, in the same transaction, cancels every waiter and the holder (with limit 1; the oldest holder otherwise), records superseded_by on them, and queues this run first in line, admitted as soon as a cancelled holder closes (at once when it has no cleanup left). Its other 409s write nothing: execution.concurrency_too_many_holders (over 50 runs to cancel), execution.concurrency_holder_unavailable (errors name the run), execution.concurrency_contended (the pool kept changing). GET reads current state; POST replay does not change as the execution advances. Inputs or fields that do not satisfy the pinned version's schemas return 422 execution.inputs_invalid with one field error per problem (`path` under `inputs.`/`fields.`, `code` such as data.required, data.type_error, data.enum, data.range or data.unknown_field, and `message`), create nothing and leave the Idempotency-Key unspent, so a corrected retry of the same action may reuse it. Other start failures (an unusable snapshot, concurrency key or vars initialization) return 422 start.invalid. Agents write live memory directly (MEM6, user decision 2026-11-13): runbooks:write on any principal credential creates status: active, with a source naming the writer: person {user_id} for a person's own credential (session or personal token), agent {token_id, sponsor_user_id} for an agent-kind personal token, service {token_id} for a service token; last_writer names whoever made the current revision. propose: true saves status: proposed instead, a proposal a person accepts or rejects. An execution access credential saves from the step run it currently claims (D40), and only if the credential that issued it holds runbooks:write (else 403 auth.scope_missing): the server derives execution ID, step run ID and actor from the claim and records MemorySaved (active; emits memory.saved) or, with propose: true, MemoryProposed (emits memory.proposed) in the execution, listed on the step's memory_saved or memory_proposed line of the execution document. Runbook scope must be its own runbook; project scope must be its own project. step_id is a relevance filter, not source identity or authorization: a step path (step IDs joined by '.', with #n loop and [key] foreach iterations) naming a step of the runbook's draft or latest published version (422 memory.invalid_step_id); an execution credential's must be the step it claims or its step key (409 memory.step_mismatch). Titles, tags and step IDs are printable text without control characters (422 memory.invalid_title, memory.invalid_tag, memory.invalid_step_id). Titles, bodies, tags and step IDs pass log-equivalent secret redaction before storage. post.description: Implemented on Postgres and Cloudflare (MEM3, MEM6). Agents write live memory directly (MEM6, user decision 2026-11-13): runbooks:write on any principal credential creates status: active, with a source naming the writer: person {user_id} for a person's own credential (session or personal token), agent {token_id, sponsor_user_id} for an agent-kind personal token, service {token_id} for a service token; last_writer names whoever made the current revision. propose: true saves status: proposed instead, a proposal a person accepts or rejects. An agent's or service's save outside a run emits memory.saved (or memory.proposed), identifiers only. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key answers the entry as first created (revision 1), or 404 to an agent or service once the entry is archived or expired. An execution access credential saves from the step run it currently claims (D40), and only if the credential that issued it holds runbooks:write (else 403 auth.scope_missing): the server derives execution ID, step run ID and actor from the claim and records MemorySaved (active; emits memory.saved) or, with propose: true, MemoryProposed (emits memory.proposed) in the execution, listed on the step's memory_saved or memory_proposed line of the execution document. Runbook scope must be its own runbook; project scope must be its own project. step_id is a relevance filter, not source identity or authorization: a step path (step IDs joined by '.', with #n loop and [key] foreach iterations) naming a step of the runbook's draft or latest published version (422 memory.invalid_step_id); an execution credential's must be the step it claims or its step key (409 memory.step_mismatch). Titles, tags and step IDs are printable text without control characters (422 memory.invalid_title, memory.invalid_tag, memory.invalid_step_id). Titles, bodies, tags and step IDs pass log-equivalent secret redaction before storage. Limits: 500 active entries and 100 pending proposals per runbook (or per project for project entries), counted separately, of which agents, services and runs may fill 450 active entries (the last 50 are people's); 20 memory writes (saves, proposals and edits) per execution; a 4 KB body. On Cloudflare a run's write that races a full quota after its run committed is kept as an archived marker (dropped: memory.limit_reached), listed on the step's memory_saved or memory_proposed line of the execution document; archives leave markers out.

post.x-claim-policy: LANG7: an assignee is guidance unless the task sets `assignment: strict`; then only the assignee (the user, or an active member of the team) with project operator-or-higher access may claim, else 403 claim.not_assignee. On an `actor: any` or `actor: human` task the assignee is a person, so an agent principal always gets claim.not_assignee (and is not offered the step); on an `actor: agent` task agents still claim by `actor`, and the assignee binds only a person taking it over. A strict assignee that resolved to nobody is resolved again against the live directory at claim time (never more broadly); when it now names the claimant, StepAssigneeResolved is recorded before StepClaimed. A person claims an `actor: agent` task only with `take_over: true`, and only while it is ready (never claimed, or its agent claim expired or was released): a live claim answers 409 claim.take_over_live_claim (a project admin may release it first); an agent principal, or a task that is not `actor: agent`, answers 422 claim.take_over_not_allowed. A take-over appends StepTakenOver after StepClaimed.

post.description: Implemented on Postgres (UP1). The caller must hold the step run's current claim (an execution access credential of the claiming family, or the claiming person). Checks the /v1/meta upload limits before issuing anything: image types (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF; HEIC is refused with upload.type_unsupported for now, D51; never SVG), PDF, plain text, Markdown, CSV and JSON files, bytes per image or file, images per step run, files per execution and storage per organization. Returns an evd_ ID and a PUT URL on the user-content origin, signed with the server key and bound to the object, the exact size and the type, valid 15 minutes. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same slot. Slots never finalized are deleted after 24 hours. Answers 503 uploads.not_configured until the server has a signing key, a user-content origin and the magic-byte table (capabilities.uploads).

post.description: Implemented on Postgres (UP1, UP2). The caller must hold the step run's current claim (an execution access credential of the claiming family, or the claiming person). Checks the stored object's size, then its type from its first bytes (magic bytes, never the name or the declared type); on any mismatch the object is deleted, the slot is rejected and the evidence is not attached (422 upload.size_mismatch, upload.type_mismatch, or upload.type_unsupported for HEIC). Images then go through the image pipeline (D51): width and height (and a GIF's first frame) are read from the file header before any decoding and refused over limits.uploads.image_max_dimension or image_max_pixels, or when the pipeline's estimated memory would exceed its budget (16-bit RGB/RGBA PNGs above about 9 MP) (422 upload.image_too_large); the image is decoded under memory limits (422 upload.image_invalid when it cannot be) and re-encoded without any metadata (EXIF and GPS location, XMP, color profiles, text), after applying its EXIF orientation. The re-encoded file replaces the upload: PNG stays PNG, JPEG stays JPEG, WebP becomes lossless WebP and GIF becomes a PNG of its first frame, so `type`, `size`, `width` and `height` describe the stored file. Each image gets a thumbnail with a 320 px long edge. The stored file plus its thumbnail must fit limits.uploads.image_bytes (422 upload.processed_too_large) and the organization's storage, which counts stored bytes (422 upload.limit_reached); either refusal deletes the upload. One image is processed at a time per server: a finalize that would wait answers 503 server.busy with Retry-After and keeps its slot for a retry. `url` and `thumbnail_url` are signed read URLs on the user-content origin, valid one to two hours. A finalized slot is returned again on retry, and concurrent finalizes of one slot answer with the same file. Reports reference finalized evidence by evd_ ID in `evidence`; `screenshot` evidence needs an image, `file` any upload.
